## Coriolis force in the coordinate frame or from a Cartesian rotation vector (`forcing/coriolis`) {#sec-ch09-coriolis}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Adds the Coriolis force $-2\boldsymbol\Omega\times\rho\mathbf v$ to the momentum.
**Switch.** `forcing/coriolis: {type, omega1, omega2, omega3, traditional}`; defaults `xyz`, 0, 0, 0, `false`.
Off unless the key is present.
**Forms.** `123`: $\boldsymbol\Omega$ given in the cell's coordinate frame. `xyz`: a Cartesian rotation vector,
projected onto the cell's frame (Cartesian, spherical-polar, gnomonic cubed sphere).
**Order.** Exact pointwise; explicit, first order in time per stage.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch09-coriolis-force.
:::

The module adds the Coriolis force evaluated at the cell centre from the stage-entry density and velocity. With
`type: 123` the three numbers are the components of $\boldsymbol\Omega$ along $x_1$, $x_2$, $x_3$ and are used as
they are. With `type: xyz` (the default) the numbers are a rotation vector in a fixed Cartesian frame, read as
`omega1` $=\Omega_z$, `omega2` $=\Omega_x$, `omega3` $=\Omega_y$, and projected once, at construction, onto the
local basis of every cell. On the gnomonic cubed sphere the force is formed in the local spherical basis and
lowered to the covariant momentum the solver stores. The option `traditional` keeps only the radial component of
$\boldsymbol\Omega$ there and is forced on for the shallow-water equation of state.

*Aliases.* "Fix Coriolis (#168)" is the cubed-sphere covariant form.

### Derivation

In an inertial frame rotating at $\boldsymbol\Omega$ the momentum equation gains $-2\boldsymbol\Omega\times \rho\mathbf v$. With $\mathbf m = \rho\mathbf v$ in an orthonormal frame, one stage adds

$$
\Delta\mathbf m = -2\Delta t\,\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf m ,
$$ {#eq-ch09-coriolis-force}

computed component by component in `CoriolisXYZImpl::forward` ([`coriolis.cpp:152-192`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/coriolis.cpp#L152-L192)) and, for
`type: 123`, in `Coriolis123Impl::forward` ([`coriolis.cpp:50-66`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/coriolis.cpp#L50-L66)). Because $\mathbf m\cdot(\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf m)=0$ the force does
no work: the energy row is not touched and needs no term [check `src/snapy_report/ch09/coriolis_check.py`,
output `coriolis_check.out`, line `[C2]`].

*Projection onto spherical-polar cells.* A Cartesian vector $(\Omega_x,\Omega_y,\Omega_z)$ has, at colatitude
$\theta$ and azimuth $\varphi$, the components

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Omega_1 &= \sin\theta\cos\varphi\,\Omega_x + \sin\theta\sin\varphi\,\Omega_y + \cos\theta\,\Omega_z, \\
\Omega_2 &= \cos\theta\cos\varphi\,\Omega_x + \cos\theta\sin\varphi\,\Omega_y - \sin\theta\,\Omega_z, \\
\Omega_3 &= -\sin\varphi\,\Omega_x + \cos\varphi\,\Omega_y ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch09-coriolis-sph}

the rows of the rotation from the Cartesian to the local $(\hat r,\hat\theta,\hat\varphi)$ basis, implemented as `omega1`, `omega2`,
`omega3` ([`coriolis.cpp:100-108`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/coriolis.cpp#L100-L108)). The rotation preserves $|\boldsymbol\Omega|$, and a rotation about $z$
gives $(\Omega\cos\theta, -\Omega\sin\theta, 0)$ [check `coriolis_check.py`, `[C3]`]. On a Cartesian grid $x_1$
is the vertical, so `omega1` $=\Omega_z$ is the $x_1$ component unchanged
([`coriolis.cpp:86-93`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/coriolis.cpp#L86-L93); `[C4]`).

*Cubed sphere.* The panel velocity is contravariant, $v^a$, and the stored momentum covariant, $m_a$. The module
maps $\rho v^a$ to the local spherical basis with the matrix of Chapter 3, forms @eq-ch09-coriolis-force there
with $\boldsymbol\Omega$ projected the same way, and maps the force to covariant components with `cs_apply_velocity_transform_`
([`coriolis.cpp:154-180`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/coriolis.cpp#L154-L180)). With `traditional` the two horizontal components of $\boldsymbol\Omega$
are set to zero, so the force is $-2\Omega_1\hat r\times\mathbf m$, purely horizontal, and only the two
horizontal momentum rows are updated.

*What is exact.* @eq-ch09-coriolis-force is exact at the cell centre for the cell-centre state; the only
discretisation is that the cell average of $\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf m$ is replaced by its centre value,
which is $O(h^2)$ where $\boldsymbol\Omega$ varies across the cell (spherical-polar, cubed sphere) and exact on a
Cartesian grid.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch09-coriolis-projection shows the projection of @eq-ch09-coriolis-sph for a rotation about $z$. The force is
a pointwise source at the cell centre: no stencil, no ghosts. It runs in every stage, explicit, after the
diffusion module in the forcing loop (@sec-ch09-framework). The projected components are computed once at
construction and stored with `register_buffer` ([`coriolis.cpp:147-149`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/coriolis.cpp#L147-L149)), so they move with the block between
devices.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch09-coriolis-projection
#| fig-cap: "Projection of a rotation about the z axis (blue arrow) onto the local basis of a spherical-polar cell at colatitude theta (sky-blue circle). The orange arrow is the radial component Omega cos(theta) and the bluish-green arrow the colatitude component -Omega sin(theta); the azimuthal component is zero."
#| fig-alt: "Half circle with the z axis, a cell centre on the circle, and two arrows from the cell along the radial and colatitude directions, labelled with their components."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch09.fig_coriolis_projection import make_fig
make_fig()
```

: Code map of the Coriolis force. {#tbl-ch09-coriolis-code}

1. `CoriolisOptionsImpl::from_yaml` checks the keys and refuses a type other than `xyz` or `123`
   ([`coriolis.cpp:19-37`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/coriolis.cpp#L19-L37)).
2. `_register_forcings_module` installs `CoriolisXYZ` for `xyz` and `Coriolis123` otherwise
   ([`register_forcing_modules.cpp:14-23`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/register_forcing_modules.cpp#L14-L23)).
3. `CoriolisXYZImpl::reset` projects $\boldsymbol\Omega$ for the grid ([`coriolis.cpp:75-150`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/coriolis.cpp#L75-L150)); an
   unsupported grid throws. On the cubed sphere it also builds the two transform matrices and sets `traditional`
   ([`coriolis.cpp:109-142`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/coriolis.cpp#L109-L142)).
4. Each stage, `forward` adds @eq-ch09-coriolis-force ([`coriolis.cpp:152-192`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/coriolis.cpp#L152-L192)).

### Limits

1. **`traditional` acts only on the cubed sphere.** It is read in the gnomonic branch only
   ([`coriolis.cpp:115-116`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/coriolis.cpp#L115-L116)); on Cartesian and spherical-polar grids, and with `type: 123`, it is
   parsed and ignored. Not tested.
2. **`123` in two dimensions** drops the $x_3$ momentum row when $n_3 = 1$ (the test `w.size(1) > 1`,
   [`coriolis.cpp:60-62`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/coriolis.cpp#L60-L62)),
   so the force then does work: $\mathbf m\cdot\Delta\mathbf m \ne 0$ in general [`[C5]`]. The `xyz` form keeps
   all three rows.
3. **Axis naming.** In `xyz`, `omega1` is $\Omega_z$, `omega2` $\Omega_x$, `omega3` $\Omega_y$
   ([`coriolis.cpp:86-88`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/coriolis.cpp#L86-L88)). On a Cartesian grid this is the $(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ order; on a sphere it is
   the Cartesian frame whose $z$ is the polar axis.
4. **Cylindrical** has a projection branch, but the coordinate type is not functional (Chapter 3).
5. **No energy check through the solver** and no convergence test of the cell-centre approximation; not measured.
